Argus is a novel framework for automatically discovering and instantiating test oracles to find logic bugs in Database Management Systems (DBMSs) using Large Language Models (LLMs).

analysis.summary: Argus automates what has been the manual part of DBMS test oracle design: inventing mechanisms that generate equivalent query pairs. It builds on the Constrained Abstract Query, a SQL skeleton with placeholders and conditions on how they may be filled; a language model proposes pairs of skeletons, their equivalence is formally proven with a SQL equivalence solver, and only then are the placeholders instantiated with synthesised snippets. On five extensively tested DBMSs it found 41 previously unknown bugs, 36 of them logic bugs.
